title: Slot coalescer and spill-gating driven by workload signals to reduce fragmentation-induced spill
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: In mixed read/write inference workloads we observed frequent small-slot fragmentation inside the KV cache leading to premature spillover to disk and elevated latency tails during bursty ingestion. This PR implements a hybrid in-memory slot coalescer plus a backpressure-aware 'spill-gating' mechanism that defers and batches spill decisions based on runtime workload signals (latency SLOs, active batch sizes, and scheduler contention), coordinated with the serving runtime's kernel selection.

What this changes: single continuous description string: (1) Slot coalescer: background and on-demand compaction that opportunistically merges adjacent free fragments into larger contiguous slots without global stop-the-world pauses. Coalescer heuristics favor eviction-friendly regions and avoid coalescing hot-resident chains; it exposes tunable thresholds for fragment age and minimal coalesced size. (2) Spill-gating: instead of immediate spill on threshold crossing, the gate consults recent workload signals (p50/p95 latency, current batch queue depth, and kernel affinity pressure). If the gate detects that spilling now would violate SLOs, it applies short backpressure (token bucket delay) and opportunistically triggers coalescing or selective pre-evictions to make room. (3) Scheduler hints: cache entries are tagged with kernel-affinity labels produced during model onboarding; the slot allocator uses these labels to prefer coalescing in regions that minimize kernel migration costs. (4) Continuous batching compatibility: the reclaim paths are non-blocking and integrated with continuous batching so that we preserve low tail latency for streaming small requests.

Why it is safe: coalescing runs with lock-free handoffs and per-region mutexes; spill-gating is conservative by default and has a 'force-spill' override for emergency OOM. We ship feature flags and knobbed rollout to avoid unexpected interference with Dedicated customers who have strict latency SLAs.

Benchmarks and results: microbench harness running mixed 60/30/10 read/write/embed workload with synthetic KV churn. Key numbers versus main @ 1M keys: - 14% reduction in eviction-induced disk spills - 6.2% improvement in p99 request latency under bursty ingestion - 9% reduction in per-token cost when batching is sustained. Warmup shows small CPU uplift (~3% median) due to coalescer background tasks; end-to-end cost wins outweigh CPU delta for heavy throughput tenants.

Rollout plan: canary (5% traffic) for 48h, monitor evictions, p99, kernel migration counters, then 25% for 24h, then 100%. Rollback: feature flag off and immediate synchronous spill if required.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for coalescer heuristics - [x] Integration tests for gating logic - [x] Performance harness and baseline results included - [x] Docs: new KV eviction strategy doc - [x] Feature flag and rollout playbook

Related: ENG-10234 design doc, ENG-10877 perf spike investigation.

review_thread: Diego: Can the coalescer starve eviction when reclaiming many tiny fragments? Aisha: Coalescer uses an adaptive budget tied to eviction backlog; if eviction pressure is high we throttle coalescing and prefer eager pre-eviction. Hannah: Unit tests look good; can you add an explicit assertion for minimal coalesced size? Aisha: Added assertion and test vectors in second commit. Omar: Spill-gate interacts with the autoscaler — if backpressure delays ingestion will autoscaler treat it as low load and scale down? Aisha: We expose a prometheus metric 'kv_spill_gate_backpressure_seconds' and recommend scaling based on request queue depth, not observed ingestion rate; included notes in docs. Diego: Approve after CI green. Hannah: Approved. Omar: Approved and merged by squash-merge.
release_notes: Introduces slot coalescer and spill-gating driven by workload signals to reduce fragmentation-induced spills and improve p99 latency under bursty ingestion. Feature gated; rollout recommended via canary.
notes: Canary observed minor kernel-migration spikes on one tenant; we adjusted coalescer affinity threshold post-canary. Ops runbook added to docs.
